rst_n.note: REVISED (this session, 3rd pass): the real klayout DRC deck found that tx_data[4]'s R=907 'extra lane' fix (see its own note) collided with rx_data[3] (R=901) on the LEFT edge where their paths run parallel on M2 for ~470um (y=430-900) -- M2 parallel runs need >=5.4um radial clearance (3.4um wire + 2.0um min space), but 907-901=6 minus the two half-widths only left 1.1um. Retreating below 901 collided with rx_data[2] (895) the same way, and every gap in the standard 847-901 lane stack is only 6.0um wide (0.6um of slack over the 5.4um minimum) -- too narrow to insert an entirely new, always-conflicting 11th lane anywhere. The real fix: tx_data[4] gets its own dedicated R=857.0 (just above the R~852-854 permanent obstruction, with 9um/5.6um-edge-gap clearance to tx_data[0]'s R=853 -- fine since tx_data[0]'s own path is RIGHT-edge-only and never angularly overlaps tx_data[4]'s TOP+LEFT-edge path, so no radial-clearance requirement applies between them at all), and lanes 2-7 (859->862.4, 865->867.8, 871->873.2, 877->878.6, 883->884.0, 889->889.4) each shift up just enough to keep 5.4um clearance from the lane immediately below; lanes 8-9 (895, 901) already had enough slack and are unchanged. Re-verified via direct db.Region separation_check (proper edge-to-edge distance, not endpoint-distance) against the permanent ground truth and all 29 other nets.

tx_data[4].note: REVISED TWICE this session. (1) lane 1/R=853.0 (the greedy packing algorithm's original assignment) collided with a real, permanent, previously-undocumented core-boundary structure at R~852-854 along the TOP edge -- moved to R=907 (6um beyond the previous highest lane at 901). (2) The real klayout DRC deck (drc.lydrc, run locally by the user against tr_1um_i2c_slave_async_reassigned.gds) then found an M1.S1 (Smin<1.4) violation at R=907: this net's TOP-edge sweep (x=-907 to 494.1) passes directly under ANOTHER permanent structure, a wide M1 block at (50,908.3)-(350,950) near the GIO_VDD_PIN area, with only 0.4um clearance to its y=908.3 bottom edge (908.3-907.9). Re-verified via direct db.Region overlap AND proper edge-to-edge separation_check (not naive endpoint-distance, which understated the true gap in the first DRC-caught violation) against the permanent ground truth and all other 29 tracked nets -- clean.
